newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian coconut oil falls, demand still poor.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian coconut oil falls, demand still poor.

text.p: Indonesian coconut oil prices softened on Monday as prolonged sluggish consumer demand continued to dampen market sentiment, traders said.

"The market continues to experience an absence of buying interest. People have switched to palm olein because it is much cheaper," said one trader, adding that demand from processing firms was also slow.
They said coconut oil was quoted at 1,470 rupiah/kg, down from last week's 1,500. Copra fell to 720 rupiah/kg against 750.
"Many traders are now concentrating on exports. We heard that 10,000 tonnes of coconut oil has been exported to Europe in May," said another trader.

They said demand for coconut oil might pick up in the local market in the coming days because of the narrow margin with palm olein. Traders said palm olein was quoted at 1,410-15 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from last Friday's close.

Traders in Manila have said coconut oil prices are likely to continue falling this week due to rising copra output in the Philippines and Indonesia and the abundance of substitutes such as palm and soyoil.
